headline: Shoriful Islam takes 7 wickets for 48 runs in Australia
summary: The left-arm pacer becomes the first visiting bowler in 33 years to claim seven wickets in a Test match on Australian soil.
details: Shoriful Islam claimed 7 for 48 to bowl Australia out for 210 on Day 2 of the second Test in Mackay. This marks the best bowling figures by a Bangladeshi bowler in an away Test match.
The feat is historically significant, as Shoriful is the first visiting bowler in 33 years to take seven wickets in a Test on Australian soil, joining West Indies legend Curtly Ambrose.
Shoriful's performance surpassed previous records, bettering Shahadat Hossain's 6 for 27 against South Africa in 2008 and Taijul Islam's 7 for 138 against Zimbabwe.
Despite his heroics, Bangladesh faces a difficult challenge. The team was bowled out for 64 in their first innings, leaving Australia with a 146-run lead.
Shoriful had already taken six wickets on the opening day, using sharp bouncers and inswingers to unsettle the Australian batters.
On the second morning, he completed his seven-wicket haul with a superb inswinging yorker to dismiss Cameron Green.
caption:
A historic feat in Australia! 🇧🇩

Shoriful Islam becomes the first visiting bowler in 33 years to take 7 wickets in a Test on Australian soil.

Shoriful Islam claimed 7 for 48 to bowl Australia out for 210 on Day 2 of the second Test in Mackay. This marks the best bowling figures by a Bangladeshi bowler in an away Test match.

The feat is historically significant, as Shoriful is the first visiting bowler in 33 years to take seven wickets in a Test on Australian soil, joining West Indies legend Curtly Ambrose.

Shoriful's performance surpassed previous records, bettering Shahadat Hossain's 6 for 27 against South Africa in 2008 and Taijul Islam's 7 for 138 against Zimbabwe.

Despite his heroics, Bangladesh faces a difficult challenge. The team was bowled out for 64 in their first innings, leaving Australia with a 146-run lead.

Shoriful had already taken six wickets on the opening day, using sharp bouncers and inswingers to unsettle the Australian batters.

On the second morning, he completed his seven-wicket haul with a superb inswinging yorker to dismiss Cameron Green.

headline: Four family members found dead in locked Rangpur home
summary: A retired schoolteacher, his wife, and their two children were discovered dead in their residence; police suspect robbery and strangulation.
details: A retired schoolteacher, his wife, daughter, and son were found dead in a locked house in the Daspara area of Rangpur city late Saturday night.
The deceased have been identified as Ganapati Chakraborty (65), his wife Pritilata Chakraborty (50), their daughter Agami Chakraborty Prarthi (23), and their son Priyam Chakraborty (12).
Police recovered the bodies of the mother and daughter from the staircase, while the father's body was found on the roof.
Investigators found household belongings scattered in disarray, leading police to initially suspect the motive was robbery.
Sanatan Chakrabarty, deputy commissioner of Rangpur Metropolitan Police, stated that they suspect the victims were strangled between Thursday midnight and early Friday.
The tragedy came to light after relatives found the family's mobile phones switched off and discovered the locked house on Saturday night.
Ganapati, a former teacher at Rangpur Zilla School, had recently started working as a homeopathic practitioner and was described by locals as friendly and courteous.
The bodies have been sent to Rangpur Medical College Hospital for autopsies, and a joint investigation by the Police, CID, and DB is underway.
